findings.claim: Invariant 1's 'a top-level profile key or an unreadable identity records unknown' is wrong for the profile shape: with a readable config, a top-level `profile` only adds a note (common:2431-37) while provider/model are still taken from -Provider/-Model or the unprofiled top-level keys (2445-2464) and written verbatim into reviewer and the ledger's model/lineage (2652-66). Codex runs the profile (it may change provider, model and effort), so the ledger records a wrong identity rather than unknown; only Resolved=false (empty fingerprint, never a parent, 2540) mitigates it. An unreadable config alone does record unknown.

**Checkpoint.** Invariant 2 holds (common:9162-68, 9241-44, 9278; harness/secrets never compared). Invariant 1 half-holds: a profile or unreadable identity does forbid fork/resume (2540) but is not recorded `unknown` (finding #1), and is codex-only (finding #4). Invariant 3 is too narrow (finding #3); invariant 4's "unchanged" is not literal (finding #5). The 0.3.0 framing and F02-* ids are an earlier task's (findings #6-#7). **Q1.** Yes, two shapes. (a) `profile = "

"` plus readable top-level `model`/`model_provider` (optionally `[profiles.

]` overriding them): Codex applies the profile, the ledger records the unprofiled values as reviewer identity/lineage - only `identity_note` and an empty fingerprint mark it. (b) A user-defined `[model_providers.openai]`: its base_url wins a fully resolved identity although "whether Codex merges it over the built-in is not verified" (common:2386-89). Scanner refusals (dotted keys, inline tables, arrays of tables, non-string values) do go `unknown`. **Q2.** No sequence found. A parent needs same provider+model+engine and an equal fingerprint; legacy entries, unresolved identities and `thread_candidate`s are never automatic parents (common:9260-89); `-Thread` is checked the same (9186-9219). One deliberate door: `-Thread` may take a non-codex run's `thread_candidate` after a kill (9198) - still reviewer+fingerprint checked. **Q3.** Not mine to certify (this run is MiMo, mimo-v1). zai-v1 still maps `medium->high, xhigh->max` (common:2753) for declared glm-5.3 (2771), sent as `-c model_reasoning_effort=...` (codex-consult.ps1:4239) and un-overridable via -CodexConfig (common:2691). Unproven: that z.ai's responses wire accepts `max` for glm-5.3 and applies it rather than erroring or dropping it; `medium`/`high` collapse to one value; `effort_confirmed` stays null forever. **Q4.** Received: the bare-JSON contract with the full reply schema (MiMo is prompt-only in caps-v1) and the last line `Consultation id: 55241ff3-...`. Not received: the effort setting - nothing in the prompt names requested/sent effort, so a reviewer can never confirm `effort_confirmed`. The bridge should prompt the effort trio (already ledgered) and record the route's request id; neither reaches me today. **Q5.** HOLD as a checkpoint (core lineage/parenting holds; claim wording drifted). Blockers: none. Unproven: Q3/Q4 and findings #1-#2. First-run checklist for a run like this: a sessions.json entry with lineage `mimo :: mimo-v2.6-pro` (`ZAI :: glm-5.3` in the brief's frame), `effort_mapping` `mimo-v1`/`zai-v1`, `usage` from the route's events, `schema_transport` `prompt-only`, and the reply ingested as validated JSON (`validation_error` empty). ## Requested checks - **RC1** (finding #1): repo root, read-only (temp config under `%TEMP%`), 2 min - `pwsh -NoProfile -Command ". ./plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1; Resolve-ReviewerIdentity -Config (Read-CodexConfigSubset 'C:/temp/ccfg/config.toml')"` on a config with `profile="p"`, `model="glm-5.3"`, `[profiles.p] model="glm-5.2"`; expect Model `glm-5.3` (drift) vs `unknown` (claim true). - **RC2** (finding #2): same invocation on a config with `model_provider="openai"` and `[model_providers.openai] base_url="https://example.invalid/v1"`; expect Resolved/Fingerprint set (drift). - **RC3** (invariants 3-5): `pwsh -File tests/run-all.ps1` from the repo root, workspace-write, 30 min, both PowerShell hosts; observation: 0 failed on the current tree.
unproven: Whether z.ai's Codex responses wire accepts model_reasoning_effort = "max" for glm-5.3 and applies it (vs rejecting the run or silently dropping the effort) - no live route evidence obtainable read-only (Q3).
Whether Codex merges a user-defined [model_providers.openai] table over its built-in provider (finding #2) - the code itself marks this unverified.
